newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FORECAST-GIB set for better 96/97 profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-GIB set for better 96/97 profits.

text.p: Belgian retail group GIB is seen posting higher 1996/97 current profit on Thursday, helped by the group's ongoing supermarket restructuring and a good performance by its U.S. DIY unit Scotty's, analysts said.

GIB shares earned mixed recommendations from stock brokers though, ranging from "speculative buy", to "fairly valued", down to "sell" because of results from burger-chain unit Quick Restaurants where 1996 net profit almost halved.
Analysts forecast a group current net profit for GIB of between 1.8 billion and 2.1 billion francs, up from about 1.3 billion in 1995/96. GIB's financial year ends on January 31.

"There will be gains from personnel costs, and in the United States they've seen operations picking up," said Ann Van Helmont at Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL). On the downside, analysts noted that in Belgium consumption had remained sluggish.

In the first half of 1996 GIB's group net profit soared to 2.5 billion francs from 0.6 billion, boosted by a 1.9 billion franc exceptional gain which followed the sale of GIB's minority stake in U.K. do-it-yourself (DIY) chain Homebase.

GIB said last August that its consolidated accounts would also show a capital gain of about 680 million Belgian francs from the sale of its interest in Sodal, the operator in Belgium of French hi-fi, photo and multi-media chain Fnac.
In full year 1995/96 GIB suffered a group net loss of 4.35 billion francs, hit by a 5.51 billion exceptional loss related to the sale of U.S. DIY unit Handy Andy.
The unit was disposed of 10 months into the 1995/96 financial year.

"There should be an improvement (in the 1996/97 results) for GB supermarkets, even if they have write-offs for Unic and Nopri (supermarket units) where sales were disappointing," said Caroline Lauwers, analyst at Bank Degroof.
She expected operating margins for the supermarket division to show a rise to 0.9 percent from 0.6 percent a year earlier.
BBL's Van Helmont noted, though, that a lot of savings from the GB restructuring had been passed on through lower prices.
Florida-based DIY chain Scotty's should also have shown an improvement in sales and operating margins.
Analysts pointed out that 1996/97 results would not contain the draining effect of loss-making Handy Andy.

In speciality retailing, the sale in January this year of GIB's loss-making department store chain Sarma to Dutch group KBB would have no impact on 1996/97 results, but prove to be a positive move for the future.
"It's good news because GIB will have a positive inflow of rent on the stores from the new owner, but the operating loss will disappear (from GIB accounts)," Lauwers said.
GIB is also seeking a partner for Inno, another of the group's speciality retailers, to boost the department store chain's buying power though has so far had no success.

As a sector, speciality retailing made up eight percent of GIB's 228-billion-franc sales in 1995/96, but only 0.2 percent of operating profit. Supermarkets accounted for 63 percent of turnover and 24.5 percent of operating profit.
Rival Belgian retailer Delhaize will announce its 1996 earnings on Wednesday.

But these should come as no surprise after the company announced in January that 1996 turnover rose 11.7 percent to 411.6 billion francs and said consolidated profit would rise between 15 and 20 percent in 1996
Its consolidated net profit was 6.81 billion, while group net profit amounted to 3.77 billion francs. U.S. unit Food Lion makes up the majority of Delhaize's turnover and profit.
One analyst said Delhaize shares were a "buy" and another considered them "rather cheap".

He said the stock should outperform in the weeks ahead, though added that investors might as well buy shares in Delhaize's U.S. unit Food Lion, which makes up the majority of the Belgian group's turnover.
Delhaize and GIB shares were unchanged at 1,910 francs and 1,530 francs respectively in a slightly easier Brussels stock market on Monday.
